headline: Microsoft unveils new Copilot super app merging AI chat, coding, and agents
summary: The redesigned app bundles three AI capabilities into a single interface, with a new 'Code' tab and rebranding of Scout to Autopilot.
details: Microsoft has officially unveiled its redesigned Copilot app, consolidating AI chat, coding, and agent functionalities into a unified interface. The app now features three distinct tabs: Home, Code, and Autopilot, aiming to streamline user workflows.

The 'Home' tab serves as the default landing experience, integrating Copilot Chat and Cowork features. It also includes a 'Today' feature, acting as a personalized dashboard for emails, meeting requests, and Teams threads, designed to help users stay organized and productive.

A notable addition is the 'Code' tab, which allows users to create and share internal apps, trackers, dashboards, or automations. This feature is powered by the same technology as GitHub Copilot and operates within a secure, sandboxed environment hosted within the user's tenant.

Previously known as Scout, the AI personal assistant has been rebranded to 'Autopilot'. This cloud-based digital teammate functions as an enterprise-grade AI assistant, capable of running tasks even while users are offline. It integrates with existing Microsoft ecosystems like Teams, Outlook, and other communication channels.

Autopilot is designed for businesses, leveraging Microsoft's identity management and Office suites. It operates within a company's tenant with its own identity, memory, and workspace, built on Microsoft IQ to understand organizational dynamics. Users can interact with it via @mentions, with built-in permissions, audit, and governance.

Microsoft is adopting a usage-based billing model for the Cowork, Code, and Autopilot features of the new Copilot app. This approach applies to agentic capabilities and the use of advanced models, allowing businesses to manage AI spend more effectively through tools like FinOps for AI.

The standard Copilot license will continue to provide access to Copilot in Chat and its integration within Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams. Microsoft employs an auto model picker for task optimization, while IT administrators can manage AI expenditures and control usage.

This latest iteration represents Microsoft's refined strategy for its AI assistant, building upon previous designs and the consolidation of its consumer and commercial Copilot apps. The company has also made significant leadership changes to centralize Copilot management.
The Home and Code tabs are slated for rollout to Microsoft's Frontier program for early access in the coming weeks. Autopilot, however, will enter a private preview phase at a later date.
